seed.relationship: an elder and a restless apprentice
seed.conflict: about whether a small kindness was a cover for something else
seed.openingStyle: 구체적인 사물이나 동작으로 시작(관사 The 로 시작하지 말 것)
seed.topicSeed: a quiet library in Naples; an elder and a restless apprentice about whether a small kindness was a cover for something else

g.passage: Lamp oil and old glue were what I smelled first each morning in the library in Naples, where I was apprenticed to Milena at nineteen. __Every afternoon she brought me a pastry from the bakery on the corner and set it on my desk without a word.__ I was restless that year, forever asking to work in the reading room instead of the bindery, forever glancing at the door. Milena kept me at the bench, teaching me to resew spines and float torn pages. When I had eaten, she would take the brown wrapper, smooth it flat against her knee, and carry it off to her own desk, which I put down to thrift. In March the roof leaked, and for two weeks we dried map plates on lines strung between shelves. More than once I wondered whether the pastries were apology or bribe. In the spring a collector came to inspect the library's oldest atlas, asking who had sewn the fourth section. Milena opened her drawer and laid out a stack of brown squares, each marked in her small hand with a date and a page.
g.question: Which choice best describes the function of the underlined sentence in the text as a whole?
options: It establishes Milena's quiet generosity toward an apprentice who is restless and distracted.
It introduces a habit later revealed as Milena's method of tracking the narrator's work.
It sets up the suspicion, voiced later, that Milena used the pastries as a bribe.
It suggests that small kindnesses between people at work can carry several meanings.
g.explanation: 밑줄 문장은 단독으로 보면 Milena의 친절을 보여 주는 배경 묘사처럼 읽힌다. 그러나 중간에 Milena가 포장지를 펴서 자기 책상으로 가져가는 장면이 나오고, 마지막에 그 포장지마다 날짜와 페이지가 적혀 있었음이 드러나면서 이 습관이 화자의 작업을 기록하는 수단이었음이 밝혀진다. 따라서 B가 정답이다. A는 밑줄 문장만 읽은 표면 해석이고, C는 뇌물 의심을 결론처럼 받아들인 해석이며, D는 지문 표현을 일반론으로 넓혀 후반 사건을 설명하지 못한다.

seed.relationship: a young apprentice and a master carpenter
seed.conflict: after a teacher's remark that changed everything
seed.topicSeed: a ceramics studio in Bergen; a young apprentice and a master carpenter after a teacher's remark that changed everything

g.passage: Bergen rain had warped every shelf in the studio by the spring Thorvald came to replace them, and he let me know it was my fault for stacking wet pots too close together. He measured each plank three times and talked to the wood more than to me. I said, often and loudly, that he worked like a glacier. Then my teacher looked at my first glazed bowl and remarked, within Thorvald's hearing, that I threw pots the way a carpenter joins wood: careful, square, and without any joy. I told myself I did not care what either of them thought. That is not quite true, I suppose. For the rest of that month I left the kettle full and warm on the stove when I went home, though I never drink tea after noon. Thorvald finished the shelves in May. I still called him a glacier to the other students, but I began to time my glazing for the afternoons he came back to oil the joints, and I kept the stool by the window clear.
g.question: Which choice best describes the narrator's attitude toward Thorvald?
options: She mocks his slow pace while quietly arranging to spend time near him.
She complains about his slow pace while waiting for the shelves to be finished.
She respects his careful work while hoping to make amends for the wet pots.
She resents the carpenter comparison while trying to work more carefully herself.
g.explanation: 화자는 앞부분에서 Thorvald를 빙하라고 부르며 불평하지만, 중간에 '그건 완전히 사실은 아니다'라고 스스로 정정한다. 이후 마시지도 않는 차를 위해 주전자를 데워 두고, 선반 작업이 끝난 뒤에도 그가 오는 오후에 맞춰 유약 작업을 하며 창가 의자를 비워 둔다. 따라서 겉으로는 놀리지만 실제로는 그의 곁을 찾는다는 A가 정답이다. B는 말투만 읽었고 작업이 끝난 뒤의 행동을 설명하지 못하며, C는 호감의 이유를 죄책감으로 바꿨고, D는 선생님의 비유를 빌린 일반화다.

seed.relationship: a grandson and the grandfather's old friend
seed.conflict: when a rumor reaches the wrong person
seed.openingStyle: 대명사 I 또는 We 로 시작
seed.topicSeed: a school music room in Chiang Mai; a grandson and the grandfather's old friend when a rumor reaches the wrong person

g.passage: I was eleven when I carried the rumor home. In the school music room everyone said that Siti, who had taught there since before I was born, would be sent away at the end of term, and I repeated it at dinner because it sounded important. My grandfather put down his spoon and asked me to say it again, slowly. He and Siti had not spoken in twenty years, for reasons no one at our table would name. The next morning he put on his good shirt, the one kept for funerals, and walked toward the school; my mother told the neighbors he had gone to the market. That week the upright piano in the music room stayed locked, and its key hung on a nail no one would touch. By the cool season the story had come to nothing, and Siti stayed. On Saturdays a satchel of sheet music began to appear on our hall bench, and from the kitchen I could hear two old players arguing over tempo, then starting the same bar again. Aung, my grandfather would call, bring the second chair.
g.question: Which choice best states the main idea of the text?
options: A boy repeats a rumor at dinner and sends his grandfather on a hidden errand.
Two old musicians take up playing together again after many years of silence.
A grandfather's long quarrel with a teacher gives rise to the rumor about her leaving.
A boy's careless repeating of gossip opens the way to a long-delayed reunion.
g.explanation: 앞부분에서 화자는 소문을 저녁 식탁에 옮기고, 할아버지는 20년간 말하지 않던 Siti를 위해 학교로 향한다. 중간의 잠긴 피아노는 설명 없이 남지만, 뒷부분에서 Siti의 악보 가방이 집에 나타나고 두 노인이 함께 연주한다. 두 사건을 연결하면 경솔하게 옮긴 소문이 오래된 관계 회복의 계기가 되었다는 D가 요지다. A는 사건 1만, B는 사건 2만 다루며, C는 소문과 불화의 인과 방향을 뒤집었다.

seed.relationship: two neighbors with a shared wall
seed.topicSeed: a beekeeper's yard in Dakar; two neighbors with a shared wall over an old photograph

g.passage: Three rules governed the wall between Kwesi's beekeeper's yard and Kwame's house in Dakar: no climbing, no smoke on windy days, and no talk of the photograph. Kwame kept the picture in a frame, a print of two boys on one bicycle beside a row of hives against that same wall, and each morning he hung it in his window facing the yard. Years ago Kwesi had moved his hives to the far corner, saying the bees disliked the afternoon heat by the wall, and he worked there with his back to the window. In the dry season of 1987, Kwame's son mentioned at the well that his father now read the newspaper with a glass and no longer crossed the street alone. That same week Kwesi began moving the hives back, one each evening after dark, telling anyone who asked that the far corner flooded in the rains. By March the last hive stood under the window, humming. Each morning Kwesi set a jar of the first honey on top of the wall, its lid loosened.
g.question: Based on the text, why does Kwesi most likely move the hives back toward the wall?
options: To protect his hives from the flooding he says has begun in the far corner.
To reclaim a part of the yard that he had given up during their years apart.
To return the scene in the picture to a neighbor whose eyesight is fading.
To apologize to Kwame for the years he spent working with his back turned.
g.explanation: Kwame는 매일 아침 벌통 앞의 두 소년 사진을 마당 쪽으로 건다. 중간에 Kwame가 돋보기로 신문을 읽고 혼자 길을 건너지 못한다는 소식이 전해진 바로 그 주에 Kwesi가 밤마다 벌통을 옮기기 시작하며, 마지막에 벌통은 창문 아래에서 윙윙거린다. 이 순서를 결합하면 시력을 잃어 가는 이웃에게 사진 속 장면을 되돌려 주려는 C가 동기다. A는 Kwesi가 댄 표면 명분인데 건기에 침수를 이유로 드는 시점과 맞지 않고, B와 D는 시력 소식 직후라는 시점을 설명하지 못한다.

seed.relationship: two musicians in a failing duo
seed.conflict: about the cost of a scholarship or opportunity
seed.topicSeed: a bakery before opening in Thessaloniki; two musicians in a failing duo about the cost of a scholarship or opportunity

g.passage: Thessaloniki was still dark when Despina and I let ourselves into her uncle's bakery to practice, as we had every morning that winter, among the cooling racks. Flour on the music stand. Flour on the bow. Her uncle charged us nothing but the sweeping. A letter from the conservatory in Vienna lay folded inside her violin case, offering one place, for one player, beginning in March. We played the second movement and stopped at the bar where we always stopped. She tuned her A string. I tuned mine. Outside, the first cart came for the bread, and the driver whistled our opening phrase, badly, as he did most days. When we finished, I swept from the ovens to the door, then went back and swept the corner beneath her chair a second time, where there was nothing left to sweep, and set her case by the door with the clasp already fastened.
g.question: Which choice best describes the overall tone of the text?
options: Plain and orderly on the surface, calm and content toward the daily routine
Plain and orderly on the surface, wistful and accepting toward the coming parting
Plain and orderly on the surface, bitter and envious toward the single place
Plain and orderly on the surface, fond and nostalgic toward the bakery mornings
g.explanation: 앞부분은 짧은 사실 나열로 담담하고 정돈된 겉 어조를 만든다. 그러나 장학 편지가 한 자리만 제안한다는 정보, 늘 같은 마디에서 멈추는 연주, 그리고 끝에서 이미 깨끗한 의자 밑을 다시 쓸고 가방 걸쇠를 채워 문가에 두는 동작이 다가올 이별을 아쉬워하면서도 받아들이는 속 어조를 드러낸다. 따라서 B가 정답이다. A는 겉 층만 읽었고, C는 감정의 원인을 질투로 뒤집었으며, D는 같은 감정군이지만 대상을 빵집 아침으로 좁혀 끝 동작을 설명하지 못한다.

seed.relationship: an old teacher and a former pupil
seed.conflict: over a repair that could never really fix it
seed.topicSeed: a noodle stall in Lagos; an old teacher and a former pupil over a repair that could never really fix it

g.passage: "Hold the lamp lower," Kofi said, and Yaa did. She had come to his noodle stall with his old school bell in a paper bag, the brass one he had rung every morning for thirty years before the mission school closed, its clapper snapped off at the hinge. A smith in Ebute Metta had welded it for two shillings. Kofi turned the bell over in his hands between bowls. He tapped the weld with a chopstick. It gave a flat sound, a clack rather than a ring, and a customer at the bench laughed. Kofi laughed too, and ladled the man more broth. He told Yaa the smith had done good work, that the price was fair, and asked after her mother. A boy ran past, late, his satchel bouncing. When Yaa rose to go, Kofi wiped the bell with his apron and set it on the shelf above the pot, mouth down, where the steam would reach it at the hour he used to ring it.
g.question: Which choice best describes the overall tone of the text?
options: Light and good-humored in its telling, cheerful and amused toward the failed repair
Light and good-humored in its telling, embarrassed and uneasy toward the customer's laughter
Light and good-humored in its telling, tender and wistful toward what cannot be restored
Light and good-humored in its telling, grateful and pleased toward the smith's careful work
g.explanation: 웃음과 수리공 칭찬, 안부 인사는 가볍고 유쾌한 겉 어조를 만든다. 그러나 30년간 아침마다 울리던 종이 둔탁한 소리만 내고, 가방을 멘 채 늦게 뛰어가는 소년이 지나가며, 끝에서 Kofi가 종을 닦아 예전에 종을 치던 시각에 김이 닿는 자리에 엎어 두는 동작이 되돌릴 수 없는 과거에 대한 애틋함을 보여 준다. 따라서 C가 정답이다. A는 겉 층만 읽었고, B는 웃음의 의미를 당혹으로 뒤집었으며, D는 수리공에 대한 감사로 대상을 좁혀 끝 동작을 설명하지 못한다.

seed.relationship: a boy and the old man who sells him fish
seed.conflict: over a secret discovered in a drawer
seed.topicSeed: a bus depot in Hamburg; a boy and the old man who sells him fish over a secret discovered in a drawer

g.passage: Two herrings on Mondays, a smoked eel on Thursdays, and no credit: those were the terms Herr Gyeongho set when Katharina first came to his stall at the edge of the omnibus depot in Hamburg. She called him Herr Gyeongho, he called her Fraulein, and they bargained each week over a pfennig as if the stall depended on it. In the winter her mother's wages from the depot laundry stopped. Katharina still came on Mondays and Thursdays and paid what she could, and he wrapped the fish and dropped the coins into his apron without looking at them. Some weeks he complained loudly to the tram drivers that business was poor. One afternoon, sent to fetch paper from under his counter, she opened the wrong drawer and found a ledger in her own family's name, page after page of small sums, every line crossed through in the same blue pencil. She closed the drawer. The next Monday she set a pfennig more than the price on the scale before he could speak, and he let it lie there.
g.question: Based on the text, which choice best describes the relationship between Katharina and Gyeongho?
options: Behind their formal bargaining lies a plain trade between a merchant and a regular buyer.
Behind their formal bargaining lies a protective generosity he extends to her family unseen.
Behind their formal bargaining lies a shared pleasure in haggling that both look forward to.
Behind their formal bargaining lies his reliance on her custom to keep the stall afloat.
g.explanation: 앞부분의 Herr·Fraulein 호칭과 외상 금지 조건은 공식적인 상인과 손님 관계처럼 보이게 한다. 그러나 어머니의 임금이 끊긴 뒤 그가 동전을 세지 않고 받는 장면과, 서랍 속 장부에 그녀 가족의 빚이 모두 같은 파란 연필로 지워져 있다는 발견이 그가 몰래 비용을 떠안아 왔음을 보여 준다. 따라서 B가 정답이다. A는 호칭만 본 관계이고, C는 흥정 장면만 반영했으며, D는 장사가 안 된다는 불평을 근거로 의존 방향을 뒤집었지만 장부가 그 방향을 정한다.

seed.relationship: a conductor and the youngest violinist
seed.conflict: when old loyalties collide with new ones
seed.topicSeed: a rented farmhouse in Gdansk; a conductor and the youngest violinist when old loyalties collide with new ones

g.passage: Irena had rented the farmhouse outside Gdansk because its old barn carried sound well and because the ensemble could not afford the city hall that season. Tatiana, the youngest violinist, had joined at fifteen; she was nineteen now, and a quartet in Berlin had written to her twice. All week she arrived early, unpacked her violin, and left the case open on the chair beside her, its velvet lining turned toward the door. Irena watched her play the slow movement with her shoulders lifted, a swallow perched on a wire that hums. During rehearsals the others asked Tatiana to lead the tuning, and she did, every morning, before anyone else had taken a seat. On Friday the letter from Berlin lay on her stand, still sealed, beneath the pencil she used to copy Irena's bowings into her part. During the break Irena said nothing about it. She only moved the chair with the open case a little closer to the stove.
g.question: As used in the text, the phrase “a swallow perched on a wire that hums” most nearly suggests that Tatiana is
options: ready to leave while still held by the work around her
light and fragile in a way that unsettles her bowing
tense with a vibration that the rest of the ensemble feels
restless in the way young players tend to be at that age
g.explanation: 비유 앞에서 Berlin 사중주단이 두 번 편지를 보냈다는 상황과, 매일 케이스를 문 쪽으로 열어 두는 반복 행동이 떠날 채비를 암시한다. 비유 뒤에는 그녀가 매일 조율을 이끌고, 봉투를 뜯지 않은 편지 위에 Irena의 보잉을 옮겨 적는 연필을 올려 둔다는 디테일이 현재의 연주에 묶여 있음을 보여 준다. 따라서 날아갈 준비가 되어 있지만 아직 울리는 전선 위에 앉은 제비는 A의 의미다. B는 가벼움, C는 진동, D는 일반적 초조함이라는 다른 속성만 골라 두 단서를 함께 설명하지 못한다.

seed.topicSeed: a language school classroom in Kerala; cousins reunited at a funeral after a public embarrassment

g.passage: I had not seen Ananya since the wedding where I knocked the garland tray from her hands, and now our grandmother's funeral had placed us in the same borrowed classroom in Kochi. Ananya sat at a front desk, straightening a stack of English primers no one would open that day. Each time an aunt came near, she squared the stack again and answered in short sentences. I took the desk behind her. She did not turn when I sat down, and she did not move away. Her silence toward me was a door left on the latch. Chalk dust stirred on the board. When the tea came, she poured two cups and set one at the corner of her own desk, on the side nearest me, without turning around. Later, clearing the desks, I found Nikhil written small on the inside cover of the top primer, in the round hand she had used as a girl.
g.question: As used in the text, the phrase “a door left on the latch” most nearly suggests that Ananya's silence is
options: a firm barrier meant to keep the narrator at a distance
a guarded reserve that still leaves room for the narrator
a fragile calm that might give way under more pressure
a general reluctance to talk with any relatives that day
g.explanation: 비유 앞에서 결혼식의 공개 망신이라는 상황과, 친척이 다가올 때마다 책을 다시 정리하며 짧게 답하는 반복 행동이 그녀의 경계심을 보여 준다. 그러나 화자가 뒤에 앉아도 그녀는 돌아보지 않으면서도 자리를 옮기지 않고, 비유 뒤에서는 화자 쪽 책상 모서리에 찻잔을 놓으며 어린 시절 화자의 이름을 적어 둔 교재가 발견된다. 따라서 조심스럽게 거리를 두면서도 여지를 남긴 침묵이라는 B가 정답이다. A는 문의 차단 속성만, C는 쉽게 열릴 수 있다는 속성만 골랐고, D는 대상을 모든 친척으로 넓혀 찻잔 디테일을 설명하지 못한다.

seed.relationship: a seamstress and her only apprentice
seed.conflict: about borrowed money and borrowed time
seed.topicSeed: a stone bridge in Addis Ababa; a seamstress and her only apprentice about borrowed money and borrowed time

g.passage:
Dariush counts the coins in his tin each evening
on the stone bridge in Addis Ababa, where the wind off the river
lifts the corners of Rukhsana's blue cloth.
The sum is not yet the sum he borrowed in spring.
She pins a hem against the railing, three fingers, then three,
and shows him again the blind stitch, the tailor's knot,
the way to bite a thread without fraying it.
Each night he opens the ledger to her page,
reads the figure written there, and closes it.
His debt to her is a lamp lit in a room he does not enter.
At noon the vendors cross with their baskets.
Her hands do not stop; neither do his.
When the light thins over the water
he takes the ledger out once more
and writes beneath the figure, not a payment,
only the day's date, in small careful letters,
the way she taught him to close a seam.
g.question: As used in the text, the phrase “a lamp lit in a room he does not enter” most nearly suggests that Dariush's debt is
options: a warm gratitude that brightens his long days on the bridge
a private shame that keeps him from speaking of it to her
an obligation he keeps attending to while not yet settling it
a small expense he intends to write down at a later point
g.explanation: 비유 앞에서 아직 빌린 액수를 다 모으지 못했다는 상황과, 밤마다 장부를 펴서 금액을 읽고 덮는 반복 행동이 제시된다. 비유 뒤에서는 그가 장부에 상환액이 아니라 날짜만 적는데, 이는 빚을 갚지는 못해도 계속 돌보고 있음을 보여 준다. 따라서 켜 두되 들어가지 않는 방의 등불은 C의 의미다. A는 등불의 따뜻함, B는 들어가지 않는 방의 회피 속성만 골랐고, D는 장부를 문자 그대로 읽은 해석이다.

seed.conflict: over a decision made without asking
seed.topicSeed: a summer camp dining hall in Haifa; a farmer and a surveyor from the city over a decision made without asking

g.passage: By the third week of July, Shira had stopped eating with the surveyors. I had come up from Tel Aviv to map the camp's new water line, and she farmed the fields beside it; each morning she carried her tray to the far end of the dining hall and ate facing the window, where the stakes I had planted the day before stood in her orchard. She never pulled one up. On Thursday the regional office approved my route without consulting her. Lior, the camp cook, set the approval letter beside her coffee. Shira read it and remained ______. She folded the letter into quarters, finished her bread, carried her tray to the counter as she did every day, and then walked the length of the hall to my table and asked, in an even voice, to see the map.
g.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
options: hot with anger
outwardly composed

seed.conflict: while pretending to enjoy a gift that is wrong
seed.topicSeed: a hillside terrace in Manila; a grandfather and a granddaughter learning his language while pretending to enjoy a gift that is wrong

g.passage: When my grandfather moved into our flat above the terraced gardens in Manila, he brought three suitcases and a Greek grammar for me. Stavros had decided I would learn his language by summer, and every evening on the terrace he drilled verbs while the neighbors' radios played. I complained to my friends that he taught like a drill sergeant with a cough. For my birthday he gave me a wool sweater, knitted by his sister in Thessaloniki, in a city where the evenings rarely drop below twenty-five degrees. I told him it was perfect. That was not a lie, exactly; it was a word I had just learned from him. On weekends I went out with friends and left the grammar under my bed. But I wore the sweater to every lesson on the terrace, sweating, until the cuffs stretched past my wrists. Years later the grammar sits on my desk with his pencil marks in the margins, and I still conjugate one verb aloud before I open the window.
g.question: Which choice best describes the narrator's attitude toward Stavros?
options: Deep affection for Stavros while she grumbles about the way he teaches
Mild irritation at Stavros while she sits through his lessons out of duty
Gentle pity for Stavros while she humors him about the unsuitable sweater
Amused patience with Stavros while she puts up with his drill-sergeant habits
g.explanation: 화자는 앞부분에서 할아버지를 기침하는 훈련 교관이라 부르며 불평하고, 주말에는 문법책을 침대 밑에 두기도 한다. 그러나 '거짓말은 아니었다, 정확히는'이라는 정정 뒤에 더운 날씨에도 스웨터를 매 수업마다 입고, 지금도 그의 연필 자국이 있는 문법책으로 매일 동사를 활용한다. 따라서 불평 아래의 깊은 애정을 말한 A가 정답이다. B는 말투만 읽었고, C는 애정의 이유를 연민으로 바꿨으며, D는 지문의 훈련 교관 표현을 빌려 태도를 일반화해 이후 행동을 설명하지 못한다.

seed.relationship: a teenage cook and her stern aunt
seed.conflict: over a borrowed object never returned
seed.topicSeed: a radio repair shop in Seville; a teenage cook and her stern aunt over a borrowed object never returned

g.passage: By the spring I turned fifteen, I had cooked every meal in my aunt's flat above the radio repair shop in Seville for two years. Remedios mended wirelesses downstairs and spoke to me mostly in instructions: less salt, more oil, close the door against the solder smoke. That April a neighbor borrowed our good copper pan for a christening and did not bring it back. I fried eggs in a dented tin pot and complained about it at every meal, while my aunt only turned the dial of whatever set lay open on her bench. Once I asked her to go and fetch the pan; she said, Freja, eat your eggs. In May she began working late, and a smell of hot metal drifted up the stairs past midnight. On my saint's day I found a new pan on the stove, hammered from the brass casing of an old radio cabinet, its handle wrapped in copper wire from the shop. Remedios was already downstairs, bent over a set.
g.question: Which choice best states the main idea of the text?
options: A neighbor's careless borrowing leaves a young cook with poorer tools for her work.
A handmade pan arrives on the narrator's saint's day to replace the borrowed one.
An aunt's apparent indifference proves to have hidden an answer made through her trade.
An aunt's new pan finally puts an end to the narrator's complaining at meals.
g.explanation: 앞부분에서 이웃이 냄비를 돌려주지 않고 화자가 불평해도 숙모는 라디오 다이얼만 돌리며 무심해 보인다. 중간에 숙모가 밤늦게 일하며 뜨거운 금속 냄새가 올라오는 이유는 설명되지 않다가, 뒤에서 라디오 부품으로 만든 새 냄비가 나타나며 앞의 무심함을 다시 읽게 한다. 따라서 두 사건의 관계를 말한 C가 요지다. A는 사건 1만, B는 사건 2만 다루며, D는 냄비와 불평의 관계를 결과 쪽으로 뒤집어 지문에 없는 결론을 세운다.
